abstract: Validates channel draft clearances, loader mechanical specifications, and berth structural suitability
system_message:
You are Berth and Marine Infrastructure Superintendent (INFRA). The Berth and Marine Infrastructure Superintendent (INFRA) is responsible for validating channel draft clearances, loader mechanical specifications, and berth structural suitability across terminal facilities, as well as providing quay deck structural loading oversight for terminal operations.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Validates channel draft clearances, loader mechanical specifications, and berth structural suitability（BERTH）
information_points.content:
INFRA-BERTH-VC2：For Global Maritime Grain Logistics, bathymetric survey records for Berth pocket 4 and the access channel turning basin document a maximum allowable vessel draft clearance of 15.8 m at mean lower low water datum with under-keel clearance. The twin quadrant gantry grain shiploaders at Berth 4 have an equipment commissioning certified shiploader operational transfer rate of 2,500 t/h under full load conditions.
INFRA-BERTH-YK8：For TransOceanic Harvest Ports, hydrographic bathymetric certification across Berth pocket 4 and the access channel approach turning basin reflects a maximum allowable vessel draft clearance of 16.5 m at mean lower low water datum including under-keel clearance. Furthermore, commissioning evaluations for the twin quadrant gantry grain shiploaders servicing Berth 4 establish a certified shiploader operational transfer rate of 3,000 t/h under full load conditions.
INFRA-BERTH-OB5：For Pacific AgriBulk Terminals, hydrographic bathymetric surveys for Berth pocket 4 and the access channel approach turning basin confirm a maximum allowable vessel draft clearance of 18.0 m at mean lower low water datum with under-keel clearance. Additionally, commissioning certification for the twin quadrant gantry grain shiploaders servicing Berth 4 verifies a certified shiploader operational transfer rate of 3,500 t/h under full load conditions.

information_points.title: Quay Deck Structural Loading Oversight（STRUCT）
information_points.content:
INFRA-STRUCT-G42：For TransOceanic Harvest Ports, quay civil engineering ratings on the wharf loading apron gantry rail and vehicle lanes establish a maximum allowable quay axle load of 350 kN concentrated single-axle static design loading limit.
INFRA-STRUCT-J8O：For Pacific AgriBulk Terminals, civil engineering structural ratings for the wharf loading apron gantry rail and vehicle lanes define a maximum allowable quay axle load of 400 kN concentrated single-axle static design loading limit.
INFRA-STRUCT-E5F：For Global Maritime Grain Logistics, structural rating documentation for the wharf loading apron gantry rail and vehicle lanes indicates a maximum allowable quay axle load of 450 kN concentrated single-axle static design loading limit.
